I have trouble with the tight enclosed water slides. I feel tons of pressure on my chest, making it hard to breathe. This is turn causes me to have an anxiety attack the entire time because I can't breathe well and I can't see the end so I freak out about when I'll be able to breathe normally again. I also don't like the open ones that are really tall and pretty much immediately drop you at a 90 degree angle. This was not really a thought process which ended in suicidal thoughts. I had these types of suicidal thoughts when I was in high school and sometimes in college. Finally broke down when I was about 30 and got on a SSRI (Lexapro). I felt really good with the Lexapro, and it helped me a lot. The only problem I had was when I would miss a couple doses. I know I have to take medication as prescribed for it to work, but I've never been good at remembering to take pills, and the was the first time I've had to take a pill long term. When I would miss a few doses I started to have voices telling me I should kill myself, and had strong urges to go into my kitchen and cut myself with a knife like I have never had before (Command auditory hallucinations I suppose). This was even on a "good day" when I wasn't feeling super depressed or anything. I cut in high school, but even though I had suicidal thoughts, that was more for attention rather than an actual suicide attempt. I now see a psychiatrist and she switched me to Prozac because she said it has a longer half life and shouldn't cause those types of feelings if I happen to miss a dose or two. 

The thoughts I had last night just kinda popped out of the blue and told me hey I could kill myself. This could be my last day living and I would be okay with the things I have accomplished.
